title: fix(app-shell): the field-permission editor shows and writes exactly what the runtime enforces for a field with no explicit rule
body:
Fixes #26597

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：权限集编辑器（Studio 访问、Setup 权限集）中，没有字段规则的字段行改为显示对象本身的“读 / 改”，灰色虚线框并注明“跟随对象”；有规则的字段照常显示，规则授予而对象未授予的格子加琥珀色圈并说明原因。单击和批量按钮只写入屏幕上真正变化的格子；“全部可读”改名“全部只读”；权限集预览列出全部字段规则。
- 为什么改：编辑器对“无字段规则”字段的显示与运行时实际执行不一致，管理员按屏幕判断会得到相反的结果（复现细节按维护者指示不公开）。
- 风险与回滚：只改界面（app-shell、i18n 文案、两篇文档）；运行时与 spec 均未改动，运行时一侧只新增一个固定现有行为的测试。回滚即还原本 PR。可见变化：未设规则的字段框变为灰色。
- 先看：`permission-slice.ts` 的 `fieldRuleCell` / `applyFieldBulk`（显示与批量写入的唯一来源）；`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` 的 `FieldRuleBox` 与 `FieldsSubTable`；`previews/PermissionPreview.tsx` 的字段列表。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/permission-slice.fieldRule-26597.test.ts`，预期 16 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The field-permission editor now shows and writes exactly what the runtime enforces for a field with no explicit rule.

- **One drawing, one source** (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/permission-slice.ts`):
  - `fieldRuleCell(entry, objectPerm)` is what a field row draws. With no entry, the row draws the object row's own Read and Edit, read through the spec's `objectPermissionGrants` (the fold the evaluator answers from, super-user bits included), and is marked inherited. With an entry, the row draws the entry's bits, read as the runtime merge reads them (`=== true`, as `fieldPermissionVote` does). A bit the entry grants and the object row does not is marked capped.
  - `fieldRuleSeed` is what a click starts from: the entry, or on a row without one exactly the bits the row draws, so a click changes only the box it lands on.
  - `applyFieldBulk` drives the three field shortcuts. Each moves the visible rows to its target and leaves a row that already draws the target as it is, so a shortcut writes only the rows whose boxes change. Clear deletes the entries, and those rows draw the object grant again. `withFieldBits` (keeps an authored `when`) moved here from the editor unchanged.
- **The editor** (`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`): `FieldsSubTable` receives the object row's permission and draws each box through `FieldRuleBox`. An inherited box is grey with a dashed edge and carries `data-field-rule="inherited"` and a tooltip. A capped box carries an amber ring, `data-capped` and a tooltip saying a holder of this set alone cannot use it. A legend line explains the grey boxes. `updateFieldPerm` and `updateFieldWhen` seed from `fieldRuleSeed`, and `bulkSetFields` calls `applyFieldBulk`. Both object layouts (the page table and the Studio matrix) render the same sub-table.
- **The preview** (`previews/PermissionPreview.tsx`, also shown per set under a position) lists every field entry the set declares, tagged hidden, read-only or editable, with a `when` named in the chip's title.
- **Strings** (`@object-ui/i18n`, `studio` namespace): `perm.field.bulk.readable` reads "Read-only all" (zh 「全部只读」) because the shortcut switches Edit off; four new keys explain the grey and amber boxes; `engine.permissionPreview.fls.readOnly` (en + zh) tags a read-only rule in the preview.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx` (the Studio bullet) and `access-recipes.mdx` (step 2 now says to set Edit off).
- **Runtime: no change.** The editor now follows the contract the spec, ADR-0066 ⑧ and the field-level-security docs already state. The runtime half is pinned by a new test, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-rule-object-grant.test.ts`.

Same-default sweep across `ui/`: the field sub-table's render, the click seed (`updateFieldPerm`), the condition seed (`updateFieldWhen`) and the bulk shortcuts are all in the one editor and are all fixed here. The preview's field list filtered entries the same way and is fixed too. `MePermissionsProvider.checkField` already defers a field without an entry to the object grant. The explain panel draws no field rows. `apps/console/src/preview-samples.ts` is sample data.

## Tests

- `permission-slice.fieldRule-26597.test.ts` (16): the six cells (no entry / read-only / editable × object Edit on / off) against the write gate's verdict, the super-user fold, the capped marks, the seed, and every shortcut's writes, including that it writes nothing for rows already at its target.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor.fieldRuleInherited-26597.test.tsx` (8): the rendered boxes and their `data-field-rule` / `data-capped` marks, and the saved payload after a click, a shortcut and Clear.
- `previews/PermissionPreview.fieldRules-26597.test.tsx` (3): every declared entry is listed and tagged.
- `field-rule-object-grant.test.ts` in plugin-security (7): the same six cells through a real `ObjectQL` over SQLite with the real `SecurityPlugin` middleware, refusals asserted on `code` + `status` (and `details.forbiddenFields` for the field gate), plus the read of a field without an entry.
- Updated: `PermissionMatrixEditor.fieldBulk.test.tsx` and `PermissionMatrixEditor.fieldWhen-25866.test.tsx` (the renamed shortcut; the Clear case now asserts the inherited mark), `previews/adminPreviews.i18n-10862-s2.test.tsx` (the new preview row in en and zh).
- Ablation (one-time, not kept, run at `ab5961d4`): with `fieldRuleCell`'s no-entry branch mutated so it no longer reads the object grant, 12 of the 24 cases in the two new editor-side files went red. The mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 → 0, blob changed) and was restored to the HEAD blob (`db141c2b`).
- One-time HTTP measurement (not kept): the six cells driven through `bootStack`'s real HTTP door by a member holding only the fixture set agreed with both pins in every cell.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not in this PR (observation, reported to the coordinator).** The object matrix draws an object row from the set's explicit row only and does not model the `'*'` wildcard, so for a set whose grant on an object comes only from `'*'` the object row and the field rows under it do not show that grant. This predates this change.
- **Dispatch vs role file.** The dispatch asked for `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands … CHANGED_PATHS`; the role file says to derive without paths so the script reads the change set from the merge base. The role file was followed.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` is private; the changeset names it with `@object-ui/console` (which ships it) and `@object-ui/i18n`, as the other app-shell changesets in `.changeset/` do.

## Verification
